dedupe_keys.name: love parade crowd disaster duisburg 2010 analysis as a systemic failure

description: This analysis of the crowd disaster at the Love Parade in Duisburg, Germany, on 24 July 2010 used publicly available videos and materials on the planning and organisation of the event to examine how and why the disaster happened, focusing on contributing causal factors and their interdependencies, not legal responsibility. The authors argue that people stumbled and piled up through a domino effect caused by crowd turbulence, also called a crowd quake, which they distinguish from panic stampedes and crowd crushes, and that this turbulence resulted from amplifying feedback and cascading effects typical of systemic instabilities. Coverage: the event venue and access routes. Access: arXiv preprint (2012). Licence: arXiv preprint terms. Caveats: a qualitative reconstruction from public video, not an official inquiry. Outcome: recommendations to prevent crowd disasters, a new scale for the criticality of crowd conditions, and a discussion of citizen science in public investigation. Simulation uses: validating crowd models for bottlenecks and event access design. Related records: the Jülich pedestrian dynamics data archive, Vadere and CrowdEgress.

name: Love Parade crowd disaster, Duisburg 2010: analysis as a systemic failure
outcomes: The analysis attributed the disaster to crowd turbulence ('crowd quake') arising from amplifying feedback and cascading effects rather than panic, proposed a scale to judge crowd criticality, and gave recommendations to prevent future crowd disasters.
resources_used: Publicly available videos and documents on the planning and organisation of the event
